title: Minimize the Maximum Waiting Time at Synchronized Traffic Lights
approach: Cars are completely uncoupled - a light serves unlimited cars and nobody blocks anybody - so every car independently picks its best light, and the late-case penalty period - r does not depend on which light was picked. Hence only L = max(lights) matters: answer = max over cars of (0 if arrivalTime[j] % period < L else period - arrivalTime[j] % period), one O(n) pass.

techniques.label: greedy
techniques.why: each car takes the widest green window; independence makes the local choice globally optimal

techniques.label: modular-arithmetic
techniques.why: the whole problem is the arrival phase arrivalTime % period inside a shared cycle

techniques.label: binary-search-answer
techniques.why: REJECTED - the title is 'minimize the maximum' and the feasibility predicate (every car waits <= W) is monotone, so a binary search compiles, but its check is just 'recompute the same max', so it is strictly the trap the audit flagged: the answer is a closed-form max, not a search over an answer space

techniques.label: exchange-argument
techniques.why: REJECTED as filler - moving a car to the max-green light never raises its wait, which is technically an exchange argument, but the dominance is immediate from the given formula rather than a proof step worth indexing

verified: python3 brute force enumerating EVERY car-to-light assignment (itertools.product) and minimising the max wait: matched all 3 samples (5, 1, 3) and agreed with the O(n) max formula on 4000 random small cases (period<=9, up to 3 lights, up to 6 cars), 0 mismatches. The exhaustive brute force is what confirms the independence claim rather than assuming it.
